verses.text: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat at the house of a leading Pharisee, and they were watching him closely.
In front of him was a man whose body was swollen with fluid.
Jesus asked the experts in the law and the Pharisees, "Is it right to heal on the Sabbath, or not?"
But they stayed silent. So he took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him away.
Then he asked them, "If your son, or your ox, falls into a well on the Sabbath, would you not pull him out at once?"
And they could not answer him.
Jesus noticed how the guests chose the best seats, so he told them this story.
"When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not sit in the best seat. Someone more honoured than you may have been invited.
Then the one who invited you both will come and say to you, 'Give this person your seat.' And you will be ashamed and have to take the lowest place.

Instead, when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place. Then, when your host comes, he will say to you, 'Friend, move up higher.' Then you will be honoured in front of everyone at the table with you.
Everyone who lifts themselves up will be brought low, and whoever humbles themselves will be lifted up."

Then Jesus said to his host, "When you give a lunch or a dinner, do not invite your friends, your brothers, your relatives, or your rich neighbours. They might invite you back, and that would be your repayment.
Instead, when you give a feast, invite the poor, those who cannot walk well, those who cannot walk, and those who are blind.
Then you will be blessed, because they cannot pay you back. You will be paid back when those who are right with God rise from the dead."
When one of the guests heard this, he said to Jesus, "Blessed is the person who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God!"
Jesus replied, "A man prepared a great feast and invited many people.
When it was time, he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, 'Come, everything is ready now.'
But they all alike began to make excuses. The first said, 'I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. Please excuse me.'
Another said, 'I have bought five pairs of oxen, and I am on my way to try them out. Please excuse me.'
Still another said, 'I have just got married, so I cannot come.'

The servant came back and reported this to his master. Then the owner of the house was angry and said to his servant, 'Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the town, and bring in the poor, those who cannot walk well, those who are blind, and those who cannot walk.'
The servant said, 'Sir, what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.'
Then the master told the servant, 'Go out to the roads and the country lanes and urge people to come in, so that my house will be full.
I tell you, not one of those who were invited will taste my feast. Many are invited, but few are chosen.'"
Large crowds were travelling with Jesus. He turned and said to them,
"If anyone comes to me and does not love me more than father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, yes, even their own life, that person cannot be my follower.
Whoever does not carry their own cross and follow me cannot be my follower.
Suppose one of you wants to build a tower. Will you not first sit down and work out the cost, to see if you have enough to finish it?
Otherwise, if you lay the foundation and cannot finish, everyone who sees it will mock you,
saying, 'This person began to build and was not able to finish.'
Or suppose a king is going to war against another king. Will he not first sit down and consider whether he can face, with ten thousand men, the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
If he cannot, he will send messengers while the other is still far away and ask for terms of peace.
In the same way, any of you who does not give up everything you have cannot be my follower.
Salt is good. But if salt loses its taste, how can it be made salty again?
It is no good for the soil or for the manure heap. It is thrown out. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear."
